data.text/markdown:
style-audit — system design

Purpose. A Python writing-style CLI that combines source-backed deterministic checks with optional, explicitly enabled editorial judgments. It reports reviewable findings; it does not rewrite prose or classify authorship. Package: 0.1.0 · Python: >=3.12
Runtime dependencies: click>=8.1, litellm>=1.106.4, pydantic>=2.10,<3, PyYAML>=6.0
Developer tools: pytest>=8.3, pytest-bdd>=8.1 Catalog counts and explorer choices come from style_audit.rules.RULES and pyproject.toml in this checkout.

data.text/markdown:
Component responsibilities

The CLI owns discovery, planning, orchestration, and exit status. The text layer owns segmentation and source-coordinate mapping. Rule modules declare policy; analyzers execute local checks or delegate selected scopes. Reporting is a terminal boundary, not part of rule evaluation.

data.text/markdown:
Input normalization and source locations

  • Markdown, reStructuredText, and plain text become prose documents. TextDocument masks code and quotations without splitting a logical unit into visible fragments.
  • Python files are parsed with the AST, never imported or run. Ordinary .py and .pyi inputs expose docstrings; recognized Marimo .py apps expose direct mo.md() strings and static f-string text. The extractor omits f-string expressions. A SourceMap maps decoded Markdown to its source positions and spelling.
  • .feature files use a syntax-aware text pass. Gherkin keyword prefixes, tags, comments, table rows, docstrings, and fenced fixtures are masked. Heading descriptions and step prose remain auditable; scenarios and step definitions are not executed or loaded.
Sentence, paragraph, section, and document scopes are declared in rule metadata. The segmenter uses punctuation and structural boundaries; it is intentionally not a full linguistic parser. The selected scope controls both what text is sent remotely and the diagnostic span returned locally.

Rule catalog

Rule IDs, engine, and scope are runtime metadata. The summary and explorer below read the canonical style_audit.rules.RULES catalog.

STE rule details

Each entry carries its diagnostic ID, engine, canonical scope, upstream source, and contextual examples. STE606 counts sentences in visible paragraphs and STE801 checks semicolons locally. Other STE entries require contextual review. The supplied PDF includes Part 2's controlled dictionary, but this catalog does not parse its entries or certify vocabulary compliance.

data.text/markdown:
Selection and execution policy

config.load_config() discovers the nearest pyproject.toml from the current working directory; --config selects an explicit file or directory. Exact IDs, prefixes, and case-sensitive filename-style globs select rules. Matching per-file selections are unioned and replace the global selection for that file; ignores always remove rules. CLI --select replaces configured global and per-file selection. Local rules run without a provider. LLM review requires selected subjective rules plus an explicit opt-in (llm.enabled, --llm, --model, or explicit selection) and a model. A deterministic-only selection never initiates a remote call. The registered scope groups rules so each request contains only its matching rules and one eligible masked unit.

Remote judging and trust boundaries

All model judging uses litellm.completion with LiteLLM's provider/model syntax. For example, openai/gpt-4o-mini uses OPENAI_API_KEY; configure other providers with their standard credentials. The model must return a JSON findings array with selected rule IDs, exact visible evidence quotes within the current unit, non-empty reasons, and optional fixes. The application validates response structure, rule IDs, fields, and evidence; provider and validation failures are operational errors, not clean results. Each scope groups its matching rules, and style-audit sends one synchronous request per eligible masked unit without unrelated document context. Generic [tool.style-audit.llm.litellm] settings may override api_base, api_key_env, custom_llm_provider, timeout, and temperature. The application adds no retries or caching. Privacy boundary: deterministic checks stay local. Opted-in LLM rules send visible prose from the selected masked unit. Python comments and executable code, Gherkin fixtures, and masked code/quotes are excluded from model input, but masking is not sensitive-data redaction. Visible docstring and Gherkin prose can still contain private information.

Diagnostics, failures, and verification

A Diagnostic carries path, rule ID, message, one-based start/end positions, evidence, and an optional fix. Reporting sorts diagnostics before rendering text or version-1 JSON.
Exit status Meaning
0 No findings
1 Findings reported
2 Configuration, input, provider, or response-validation error
The suite combines focused unit tests with pytest-bdd acceptance scenarios. Tests use controlled providers; the Decision adapter also has a local HTTP route smoke test. No test requires provider credentials. The installed command is style-audit; python -m style_audit exposes the same CLI. Run or export this report from the repository root: 
uv run marimo edit notebooks/system_design.py
uv run marimo run notebooks/system_design.py
uv run marimo export html notebooks/system_design.py -o /tmp/style-audit-system-design.html
Implementation references: src/style_audit/cli.py, config.py, docstrings.py, marimo_docs.py, gherkin.py, text.py, rules/no-ai-slop.yaml, rules/readability.yaml, rules/technical-english.yaml, rule_catalog.py, src/style_audit/rules/__init__.py, deterministic.py, llm.py, decision_api.py, models.py, and reporting.py. The checked-in architecture guide records the package contracts.
